The *Pārājikakaṇḍa* of the *Katthapaññattivāra* (Pvr 2.9) is a catechismal section of the *Parivāra*, the final collection of the Theravāda *Vinaya Piṭaka* [SuttaCentral]. It forms part of the interrogative analysis of the *Bhikkhunī Vibhaṅga*, explaining the origins, promulgations, and conditions surrounding the Vinaya rules governing Buddhist nuns, functioning in parallel to the corresponding inquiry on the monks' code in Pvr 1.1 [SuttaCentral]. An English translation of the section has been produced by Bhikkhu Brahmali [SuttaCentral].

Computational text-reuse analysis shows substantial internal repetition within the *Vinaya Piṭaka*, with 2,576 matching passages across 42 Pali texts [DharmaNexus]. Its closest textual correspondences occur with other *Katthapaññattivāra* sections, notably Pvr 2.1 (762 matches, sharing up to §9.0–22.9 with §25.0–38.10), Pvr 1.1 (780 matches), and Pvr 1.9 (383 matches) [DharmaNexus]. Further Pali reuse is identified in the *Bhikkhunī Pātimokkha*, specific rules of the *Bhikkhunī Vibhaṅga* (such as Saṅghādisesas 6 and 11), the *Antarapeyyāla* (Pvr 4), the *Samuccayavāra* (Pvr 1.8 and Pvr 2.8), and the commentary *Parivāra-aṭṭhakathā* [DharmaNexus]. Across languages, DharmaNexus registers alignments with Northern Vinaya materials, including the Tibetan *Bhikṣuṇīprātimokṣasūtra* (D0004), the *Vinaya-uttaragrantha* (D0007A), the *Vinayasūtravṛtti* (D4119-2), and the *Ekottarakarmaśataka* (D4118) [DharmaNexus].

All candidate passages in the retrieved dossier mention the *Pārājikakaṇḍa* as the first major division of the *Suttavibhaṅga* (*Pārājikapāḷi*), cite its commentary in the *Samantapāsādikā*, or discuss *pārājika* rules generally, rather than this specific analytical catechism of the *Parivāra*.
